record.paper_title: Non-Supersymmetric (but) Extreme Black Holes, Scalar Hair and Other Open Problems
record.context_brief: String-theory sources for primary scalar hair
record.original_question: Does full string theory contain microscopic sources or allowed elementary degrees of freedom that can produce primary scalar hair, or should the absence of such sources mean that string theory excludes low-energy supergravity solutions with primary scalar hair and their associated naked singularities?

evidence.quote: Something similar happens with primary scalar hair: SUSY does not constrain its existence.

With primary scalar hair the situation is not so clear. In fact, one could argue that there are no sources within string theory for primary scalar hair and, as such, it should be impossible to build string theory solutions with primary scalar hair.
Clearly more work on this area is needed to clarify these crucial issues.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Consider the low-energy effective field theory limit of string theory, which (in a given background) takes the form of a supergravity action coupled to a finite collection of moduli/dilaton-like scalar fields, gauge fields and fermions, together with a spectrum of fundamental microscopic objects (strings, D-branes, NS5-branes, Kaluza-Klein modes, momentum modes, bound states thereof). A static, asymptotically flat, four-dimensional supergravity solution is said to carry "primary scalar hair" if it possesses one or more scalar charges Σ_i (defined via the asymptotic expansion φ_i(r) = φ_i^∞ + Σ_i/r + O(1/r^2) of the canonically normalized scalars at spatial infinity) that are independent free parameters of the solution, not fixed as functions of the mass, angular momentum, and conserved gauge charges (in contrast to "secondary hair," in which Σ_i is determined by these other charges). Many such low-energy solutions exhibit naked singularities.

Problem. Determine whether full (non-perturbative) string theory contains microscopic sources—i.e., admissible configurations of its elementary degrees of freedom (fundamental strings, D-branes, solitonic branes, and their bound states), possibly together with consistent boundary conditions on the moduli at infinity—that can act as sources for primary scalar hair in the above sense. Equivalently: either (a) exhibit an explicit microscopic string-theoretic construction whose long-distance fields realize a supergravity solution with a non-trivial independent scalar charge Σ_i not fixed by the mass and gauge charges; or (b) prove that no such microscopic source exists, thereby establishing that the corresponding low-energy supergravity solutions with primary scalar hair (and their associated naked singularities) are excluded from the string-theory landscape.
artifact.category_tag: String theory black holes and scalar hair
artifact.status_search_result: The question of whether string theory admits microscopic sources for primary scalar hair remains unresolved. Recent work continues to construct gravitational solutions with primary scalar hair in modified gravity (e.g. Beyond Horndeski, Einstein-Weyl-Maxwell-conformal scalar theories) but does not produce an explicit microscopic string-theoretic source. Likewise, ongoing programs on black-hole "hair modes" and microscopic counting in string theory have not settled whether primary scalar hair can arise from fundamental string degrees of freedom, nor have they ruled it out. No definitive answer was found in the search.

status_evidence.title: Black holes with primary scalar hair
status_evidence.snippet: Explicit black holes endowed with primary scalar hair presented within the shift-symmetric subclass of Beyond Horndeski theories.
status_evidence.claim: Primary scalar hair black holes continue to be constructed in modified-gravity settings, but not from string-theoretic microscopic sources.

status_evidence.title: Black hole with primary scalar hair in Einstein-Weyl-Maxwell-conformal scalar theory
status_evidence.snippet: A newly charged black hole solution featuring primary scalar hair has been obtained numerically.
status_evidence.claim: Recent constructions of primary-scalar-hair solutions remain at the level of effective field theory, not microscopic string theory.

status_evidence.title: Unlocking Black Hole Secrets: The Role of Hair Modes in String Theory
status_evidence.snippet: Research identifies black-hole hair modes as smooth normalizable degrees of freedom outside the horizon affecting microscopic properties.
status_evidence.claim: String-theoretic accounts of black hole hair are active research, with no conclusive identification of microscopic sources for primary scalar hair.
